description:
Found while doing fz-5xp.38, and fixed with it.

    fnp classify(x) when -x > 0.0, do: :negative
    fnp classify(_), do: :other

    classify(-5.5)   interp :other      run :negative   build :negative

`-(-5.5)` is `5.5`, which is `> 0.0`, so run and build were right and interp
was wrong -- and wrong SILENTLY, by falling through to the next clause rather
than failing.

CAUSE: `dispatch_exec.rs` evaluated guard negation as
`AnyValue::Int(-guard_int(v)?)`, and `guard_int` is `as_i64`, which is `None`
for a float. The `?` then abandoned the guard, which reads as "this clause did
not match".

That made negation's THIRD implementation: the expression evaluator
(`binop::eval_unop`) handled both lanes correctly all along, native codegen
handled one until fz-5xp.33 gave it the other, and the guard evaluator handled
one. Guards now call `eval_unop`, so there is one answer.

It was invisible until fz-5xp.33: before that, a float guard negation aborted
on run and build, so there was nothing for interp to disagree WITH.

Pinned by behavior/negate_guard on all three doors.
title: [BUG] Guard negation was integer-only in the interpreter
